open_questions: M5 doctrine NOT applied to sparse: the documented M5 starting point (BK=128 / 2×2 simdgroups / Morton walk) lives ONLY in the dense NAX kernel (NAAttentionKernel.cpp:310-314). The sparse kernel is pinned to BQ=BK=32, WM=2 (2 simdgroups, per-Q-tile TG dispatch, NO Morton walk) for mask-block faithfulness. A larger-BK / 2×2 / Morton sparse variant was NEVER tried — untested whether it could win on M5. RE-TEST candidate.

WM=1 pin conflates correctness with perf: mfa_sparse_attention.cpp:855-857 rejects WM=1 as '3-4× slower AND wrong-but-finite (Category-A)'. Is the wrong-but-finite a fixable bug (which would re-open a WM sweep) or an intrinsic occupancy loss? The two claims should be separated before treating WM=2 as settled.

BT16 never given a native NAX kernel: BT is structurally pinned 32; sub-32 mask granularity routes to scalar/SDPA (the 5.5× footgun). Open whether BT16 is intrinsically infeasible for cooperative-tensor mask faithfulness or merely unbuilt.

bf16 coverage is measurement-limited, not kernel-limited: bf16 is just T=bfloat with no kernel change (mfa_sparse_attention.cpp:1211-1216), yet the gate admits only 1 causal + 1 non-causal bf16 region (lcsa_nax.py:372-388). Likely more winning bf16 cells exist — under-measured.

Density-only routing ignores mask STRUCTURE: win magnitude spans 2.5×→8.23× at similar density (sliding-window ≫ random), and a structured_window_probe codegen already exists (mfa_sparse_attention.cpp:846-881) but is NOT routed by the public gate. A structure-aware gate could route more aggressively / avoid marginal high-density cells.
